findings.title: Keep index construction serialized for each namespace/resource key
findings.body: The cache mutex now protects only publication, so GetIndex returns nil while an index is being built. Concurrent searches, or a search racing with the write-event handler, can therefore build separate indexes for the same key. For in-memory indexes, the last publication replaces the other index and can discard updates already applied by the event handler; for file-backed indexes, both builds attempt to create the same directory and one can fail. Use per-key locking or singleflight around the cache recheck, construction, and publication while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

findings.title: Synchronize TotalDocs with index-cache writes
findings.body: The new startup log calls TotalDocs after the write-event consumer has been started. TotalDocs iterates the Bleve backend's cache map without taking cacheMu, while that consumer can build and publish an index for a new namespace or one skipped by InitMinCount. This introduces an unsynchronized map read/write and can terminate the process with 'concurrent map iteration and map write' during startup. Protect TotalDocs's cache traversal with the cache read lock.

findings.title: Preserve the stopped-service guard when removing lazy initialization
findings.body: Removing the Init checks from request handlers also removes their shutdown guard: Stop sets initErr to 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped', and previously Init returned that error to subsequent requests. Now Create, Update, Delete, and the other handlers continue using the backend after Stop. The SQL backend's Stop only cancels its pollers, so these writes can still succeed without being propagated to watchers or search indexes. Retain a separate lifecycle-state check even though initialization is now eager.
